title: End behavior of an even-degree polynomial
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

Which statement describes the end behavior of h(x)=9−x³+4x⁶?

correct.rationale: The leading term is 4x⁶ (degree 6 is even, coefficient 4 is positive), so h(x)→∞ as x→∞ and as x→−∞.

wrong.text: h(x)→−∞ in both directions
wrong.rationale: The sign is taken from the −x³ term instead of the leading term 4x⁶. An even degree with a negative coefficient would give −∞ at both ends, but the actual leading coefficient is +4.
wrong.error_pattern: reads the sign from a lower-degree term

wrong.text: h(x)→−∞ as x→∞ and h(x)→∞ as x→−∞
wrong.rationale: This treats −x³ as the leading term (odd degree 3, coefficient −1), which falls to the right and rises to the left. The highest power is x⁶, not x³.
wrong.error_pattern: uses the wrong term as the leading term

wrong.text: h(x)→∞ as x→∞ and h(x)→−∞ as x→−∞
wrong.rationale: This mixes terms: it reads the odd exponent 3 from x³ but the positive coefficient 4 from the leading term. With degree 6 (even), both ends go the same direction.
wrong.error_pattern: mixes degree parity and sign from different terms

change_note: New even-degree polynomial with positive leading coefficient, terms written out of order, so the leading term must be identified.

title: End behavior of an odd-degree polynomial with a large even term
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

A polynomial function is given by m(x)=−9x⁴+2x⁷+x. Which description of its graph is correct?

correct.text: The graph rises to the right and falls to the left
correct.rationale: The leading term is 2x⁷ (degree 7 is odd, coefficient 2 is positive), so m(x)→∞ as x→∞ and m(x)→−∞ as x→−∞.

wrong.text: Both ends of the graph fall
wrong.rationale: This takes −9x⁴ as the leading term because it has the largest coefficient in absolute value. The degree controls end behavior, and the highest degree is 7, from 2x⁷.
wrong.error_pattern: picks the term with the largest coefficient

wrong.text: Both ends of the graph rise
wrong.rationale: The positive leading coefficient 2 is used, but the behavior of an even-degree polynomial is applied. The degree is 7 (odd), so the two ends go in opposite directions.
wrong.error_pattern: ignores odd degree

wrong.text: The graph falls to the right and rises to the left
wrong.rationale: Odd degree is recognized, but the sign is taken as negative (from the −9 in −9x⁴). The leading coefficient is +2, so the right end rises, not falls.
wrong.error_pattern: wrong sign of leading coefficient with odd degree

change_note: Odd-degree positive polynomial where a lower-degree term has a larger coefficient; verbal answer choices.

title: End behavior from a factored polynomial
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

Which statement describes the end behavior of p(x)=−3(x−1)²(x+2)(x−4)?

correct.rationale: Multiplying the factors gives degree 2+1+1=4 with leading coefficient −3, an even degree with a negative coefficient, so p(x)→−∞ as x→∞ and as x→−∞.

wrong.text: p(x)→∞ at both ends
wrong.rationale: The even degree 4 is found, but the −3 is ignored. A negative leading coefficient makes both ends go down, not up.
wrong.error_pattern: ignores the negative leading coefficient

wrong.text: p(x)→−∞ as x→∞ and p(x)→∞ as x→−∞
wrong.rationale: Counts only the three distinct factors, getting degree 3 instead of 4, since (x−1) appears squared. With an odd degree and coefficient −3 the right end falls and the left end rises, but the true degree is even.
wrong.error_pattern: drops the repeated factor when finding degree

wrong.text: p(x)→∞ as x→∞ and p(x)→−∞ as x→−∞
wrong.rationale: Counts three distinct factors for an odd degree of 3 and also ignores the −3. The true degree is 4 and the leading coefficient is −3.
wrong.error_pattern: drops the repeated factor and ignores the sign

change_note: Factored form with a repeated factor; degree and sign must be read from the factors.

title: Vertical asymptotes of a rational function
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

Let r(x)=(x−10)/(x²+3x−28). At which values of x does the graph of r have vertical asymptotes?

correct.rationale: The denominator factors as (x+7)(x−4). Neither factor cancels the numerator x−10, so both x=−7 and x=4 are vertical asymptotes.

wrong.text: x=10 only
wrong.rationale: x=10 is the zero of the numerator, which gives an x-intercept of the graph, not a vertical asymptote.
wrong.error_pattern: uses the numerator zero

wrong.text: x=7 and x=−4
wrong.rationale: The denominator is factored as (x−7)(x+4), which expands to x²−3x−28, not x²+3x−28. The signs of the roots are reversed; the correct roots are −7 and 4.
wrong.error_pattern: reverses the signs of the denominator zeros

wrong.text: x=4 only
wrong.rationale: x=4 is a zero of the denominator, but x=−7 is also a zero of (x+7)(x−4) and does not cancel with the numerator, so it is a vertical asymptote too.
wrong.error_pattern: finds only one denominator zero

change_note: Different rational function, numbers and wording; distractors from numerator zero, reversed signs and a missing zero.

title: Vertical asymptote versus hole
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

The function t(x)=(x+8)/(x²−x−72) is defined wherever its denominator is nonzero. Determine where its graph has vertical asymptotes.

correct.rationale: The denominator factors as (x−9)(x+8), so t(x)=1/(x−9) for x≠−8. The factor x+8 cancels, so x=−8 is a hole and only x=9 is a vertical asymptote.

wrong.text: At x=−8 and x=9
wrong.rationale: Both denominator zeros are used without checking for cancellation. The factor x+8 appears in the numerator too, so x=−8 is a hole, not an asymptote.
wrong.error_pattern: does not check for canceled factors

wrong.text: Only at x=−8
wrong.rationale: x=−8 is the zero shared by numerator and denominator, which produces a hole. The only noncanceled denominator zero is x=9.
wrong.error_pattern: selects the canceled factor instead of the remaining one

wrong.text: At x=8 and x=−9
wrong.rationale: The denominator is factored as (x−8)(x+9), which expands to x²+x−72, not x²−x−72. The signs of the roots are reversed, and the cancellation is also missed.
wrong.error_pattern: reverses the signs of the denominator zeros

change_note: A canceled common factor means one denominator zero is a hole, testing the 'noncanceled' condition.

title: Vertical asymptotes with numerator factors
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

For the rational function w(x)=(x²−25)/(x²−x−56), which are the vertical asymptotes of its graph?

correct.rationale: The denominator factors as (x−8)(x+7) and the numerator is (x−5)(x+5). No factors cancel, so the vertical asymptotes are x=−7 and x=8.

wrong.text: x=−5 and x=5
wrong.rationale: These are the zeros of the numerator x²−25, which are x-intercepts, not vertical asymptotes.
wrong.error_pattern: uses the numerator zeros

wrong.text: x=−8 and x=7
wrong.rationale: The denominator is factored as (x+8)(x−7), which expands to x²+x−56, not x²−x−56. The signs of the roots are reversed.
wrong.error_pattern: reverses the signs of the denominator zeros

wrong.text: x=8 only
wrong.rationale: x=8 is a zero of the denominator, but x=−7 also makes (x−8)(x+7) equal to 0 and nothing cancels it, so it is also a vertical asymptote.
wrong.error_pattern: finds only one denominator zero

change_note: Quadratic numerator and denominator, no cancellation.

title: Hole from a removable factor
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

Consider g(x)=(x²−x−6)/(x−3), defined for x≠3. Which description of the graph of g is correct?

correct.rationale: For x≠3, g(x)=(x−3)(x+2)/(x−3)=x+2. The factor x−3 cancels, and the missing point has y-value 3+2=5, so there is a hole at (3,5).

wrong.text: x=3 is a vertical asymptote.
wrong.rationale: A vertical asymptote needs a noncanceled denominator zero. The factor x−3 cancels completely, so x=3 is a hole.
wrong.error_pattern: treats a canceled factor as an asymptote

wrong.text: There is a hole at (−2,0).
wrong.rationale: x=−2 is the zero of the remaining factor x+2, which is an x-intercept. The hole is at the canceled factor, x=3.
wrong.error_pattern: uses the remaining zero as the hole

wrong.text: There is a hole at (3,0).
wrong.rationale: The hole's x-coordinate 3 is right, but the y-value is found by evaluating the original numerator at 3 (9−3−6=0). It should be found from the simplified expression: 3+2=5.
wrong.error_pattern: evaluates the unsimplified numerator for the y-coordinate

change_note: Quadratic numerator with a non-obvious factorization; distractors include a wrong y-coordinate.

title: Hole coordinates from a factorable numerator
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

A function is defined by k(x)=(2x²+x−3)/(x−1) for x≠1. Which is true of the graph of k at x=1?

correct.rationale: The numerator factors as (2x+3)(x−1), so k(x)=2x+3 for x≠1. The y-value of the hole is 2(1)+3=5.

wrong.text: A hole at (1,0)
wrong.rationale: The numerator evaluates to 2+1−3=0 at x=1, but that is the unsimplified 0/0 form. The hole's y-value comes from the simplified function: 2(1)+3=5.
wrong.error_pattern: uses the numerator's value as the y-coordinate

wrong.text: A hole at (−3/2,0)
wrong.rationale: x=−3/2 is the zero of the remaining factor 2x+3, which is an x-intercept. The hole is at the canceled factor x=1.
wrong.error_pattern: uses the remaining zero as the hole

wrong.text: A vertical asymptote
wrong.rationale: The factor x−1 cancels with the numerator, so x=1 is a hole, not a vertical asymptote.
wrong.error_pattern: treats a canceled factor as an asymptote

change_note: Leading coefficient other than 1 in the numerator; different function and distractor set.

title: Hole and asymptote in the same function
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

Let p(x)=(x−5)/(x²−25) for x≠5 and x≠−5. Which statement is true?

correct.text: The graph has a hole at (5,1/10) and a vertical asymptote at x=−5.
correct.rationale: For x≠5, p(x)=(x−5)/((x−5)(x+5))=1/(x+5). The factor x−5 cancels, leaving a hole at x=5 with y=1/10, and x+5 stays in the denominator, giving a vertical asymptote at x=−5.

wrong.text: The graph has holes at x=5 and x=−5 and no vertical asymptote.
wrong.rationale: Only the factor x−5 cancels. The factor x+5 remains in the denominator after simplifying, so x=−5 is a vertical asymptote.
wrong.error_pattern: treats every denominator zero as a hole

wrong.text: The graph has a hole at (5,0) and a vertical asymptote at x=−5.
wrong.rationale: The hole's location x=5 and the asymptote are right, but the y-value of the hole must come from the simplified function 1/(x+5), which gives 1/10 at x=5, not 0.
wrong.error_pattern: uses the numerator value as the hole's y-coordinate

wrong.text: The graph has vertical asymptotes at x=5 and x=−5 and no holes.
wrong.rationale: The factor x−5 cancels with the numerator, so x=5 is a hole. Only x=−5 is a vertical asymptote.
wrong.error_pattern: treats every denominator zero as an asymptote

change_note: Function with both a hole and an asymptote, and a nonzero hole value that is a fraction.

title: Reading shifts and a vertical shrink
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

If g(x)=(1/2)f(x+4)−6, which transformation takes the graph of f to the graph of g?

correct.text: Left 4, vertical shrink by factor 1/2, down 6
correct.rationale: x+4 inside f shifts left 4, the factor 1/2 outside shrinks vertically by 1/2, and −6 outside shifts down 6.

wrong.text: Right 4, vertical shrink by factor 1/2, down 6
wrong.rationale: This reverses the horizontal shift. Replacing x with x+4 moves the graph left 4, not right.
wrong.error_pattern: reverses the direction of the horizontal shift

wrong.text: Left 4, vertical stretch by factor 2, down 6
wrong.rationale: This uses the reciprocal of the multiplier. Multiplying outputs by 1/2 halves them, which is a shrink by 1/2, not a stretch by 2.
wrong.error_pattern: reverses stretch and shrink

wrong.text: Left 6, vertical shrink by factor 1/2, down 4
wrong.rationale: This swaps the two shifts. The +4 inside f gives the horizontal shift (left 4) and the −6 outside gives the vertical shift (down 6).
wrong.error_pattern: swaps the horizontal and vertical shifts

change_note: No reflection; includes a shrink factor of 1/2 and a leftward shift.

title: Reflection across the y-axis with an outside multiplier
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

Let g(x)=3f(−x)+2. Describe how the graph of f is changed to obtain the graph of g.

correct.text: Flip over the y-axis, triple every output, then move up 2
correct.rationale: The −x inside f flips the graph over the y-axis, the factor 3 outside multiplies every output by 3 (a vertical stretch), and +2 outside shifts up 2.

wrong.text: Flip over the x-axis, triple every output, then move up 2
wrong.rationale: The negative sign is inside f (f(−x)), which flips the graph over the y-axis. A flip over the x-axis would need a negative outside, as in −f(x).
wrong.error_pattern: confuses the two reflections

wrong.text: Flip over the y-axis, divide every x-value by 3, then move up 2
wrong.rationale: The multiplier 3 is outside f, so it scales the outputs (vertical stretch by 3). Dividing x-values by 3 (a horizontal shrink by 1/3) would come from f(3x).
wrong.error_pattern: treats an outside multiplier as an inside one

wrong.text: Flip over the y-axis, triple every output, then move left 2
wrong.rationale: The +2 is added outside f, so it shifts the graph up 2. A shift left 2 would come from f(x+2).
wrong.error_pattern: treats an outside constant as a horizontal shift

change_note: Reflection inside the function with a different multiplier and distractors about inside versus outside.

title: Horizontal compression requiring factoring
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

If g(x)=−f(2x−6), which transformation takes the graph of f to the graph of g?

correct.text: Reflect across the x-axis, horizontal shrink by factor 1/2, right 3
correct.rationale: Writing 2x−6=2(x−3) gives g(x)=−f(2(x−3)). The factor 2 compresses horizontally by 1/2, x−3 shifts right 3, and the outside negative reflects across the x-axis.

wrong.text: Reflect across the x-axis, horizontal shrink by factor 1/2, right 6
wrong.rationale: The shift is read directly from the −6 without factoring out the 2. Since 2x−6=2(x−3), the shift is right 3, not 6.
wrong.error_pattern: does not factor out the horizontal scale before reading the shift

wrong.text: Reflect across the x-axis, horizontal stretch by factor 2, right 3
wrong.rationale: The inside factor 2 makes the graph reach each output at half the x-distance, which is a horizontal shrink by 1/2, not a stretch by 2.
wrong.error_pattern: reverses horizontal stretch and shrink

wrong.text: Reflect across the y-axis, horizontal shrink by factor 1/2, right 3
wrong.rationale: The negative sign is outside f, −f(…), which negates outputs and reflects across the x-axis. A reflection across the y-axis would need a negative inside the argument.
wrong.error_pattern: confuses the two reflections

change_note: Inside linear expression needs factoring to read the shift; combined with a reflection.

title: Second differences identify a quadratic
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

For equally spaced inputs x=0, 1, 2, 3, 4, a table gives y=3, 4, 7, 12, 19. Which model type is most appropriate, and why?

correct.text: Quadratic, because the second differences are constant (all equal to 2)
correct.rationale: The first differences are 1, 3, 5, 7 and the second differences are 2, 2, 2. Constant nonzero second differences indicate a quadratic model.

wrong.text: Linear, because the first differences (1, 3, 5, 7) increase by a steady amount
wrong.rationale: A linear model needs constant first differences. These differ (1, 3, 5, 7), so the model is not linear; the steady change in the first differences is what indicates a quadratic.
wrong.error_pattern: confuses a steady change in first differences with constant first differences

wrong.text: Exponential, because the outputs increase by a larger amount each step
wrong.rationale: An exponential model needs a constant ratio between consecutive outputs. Here the ratios are 4/3, 7/4, 12/7, 19/12, which are not equal.
wrong.error_pattern: assumes any accelerating growth is exponential

wrong.text: Cubic, because the first differences are not constant
wrong.rationale: Nonconstant first differences only rule out a linear model. The second differences are already constant (2, 2, 2), which identifies a quadratic, not a cubic.
wrong.error_pattern: stops at nonconstant first differences and jumps to a higher degree

change_note: Concrete table in place of an abstract description; reasoned choices.

title: Third differences identify a cubic
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

Equally spaced inputs x=0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 produce the outputs 0, −1, 4, 21, 56, 115. Which kind of function best fits these values?

correct.text: A cubic model; the third differences are all 6
correct.rationale: The first differences are −1, 5, 17, 35, 59; the second differences are 6, 12, 18, 24; the third differences are 6, 6, 6. Constant third differences indicate a cubic.

wrong.text: A quadratic model; the second differences 6, 12, 18, 24 grow steadily
wrong.rationale: A quadratic needs constant second differences. These are 6, 12, 18, 24, which are not equal, so the model is not quadratic.
wrong.error_pattern: confuses a steady change in second differences with constant second differences

wrong.text: An exponential model; the first differences keep growing
wrong.rationale: An exponential ab^x with a≠0 and b>0 never outputs 0 or changes sign, but the outputs here are 0 at x=0 and −1 at x=1. The consecutive ratios are also not constant.
wrong.error_pattern: assumes growing differences mean exponential

wrong.text: A quartic model; the third differences are not zero
wrong.rationale: Nonzero constant third differences identify a cubic. A quartic model would show constant fourth differences, and here the third differences are already constant.
wrong.error_pattern: uses 'nonzero' to push the degree one higher

change_note: Third differences instead of second; negative and zero outputs rule out exponential.

title: Quadratic with negative leading coefficient from a table
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

A ball's height h (in feet) is recorded every half second: for t=0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2 seconds, h=2, 8, 12, 14, 14. Which model type is most appropriate for h as a function of t?

correct.text: Quadratic, with a negative leading coefficient
correct.rationale: The first differences are 6, 4, 2, 0 and the second differences are −2, −2, −2. Constant second differences indicate a quadratic, and the negative value means the leading coefficient is negative.

wrong.text: Quadratic, with a positive leading coefficient
wrong.rationale: The model type is right, but the second differences are −2 (negative), so the parabola opens downward and the leading coefficient is negative.
wrong.error_pattern: ignores the sign of the second differences

wrong.text: Linear, with a positive slope
wrong.rationale: The outputs rise overall, but a linear model needs constant first differences. These are 6, 4, 2, 0.
wrong.error_pattern: reads 'increasing' as linear

wrong.text: Cubic, with a negative leading coefficient
wrong.rationale: The negative sign is right, but the second differences are already constant (−2, −2, −2), which means degree 2. A cubic would need constant third differences.
wrong.error_pattern: chooses a degree above the one the differences show

change_note: Context table with a downward-opening quadratic; asks for the sign of the leading coefficient.

title: Remainder Theorem with a positive root
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

When p(x)=x³+4x²−5x+6 is divided by x−3, what is the remainder?

correct.rationale: By the Remainder Theorem the remainder is p(3)=27+36−15+6=54.

wrong.rationale: This evaluates p(−3) instead of p(3): −27+36+15+6=30. Dividing by x−3 gives remainder p(3).
wrong.error_pattern: evaluates at the opposite sign

wrong.rationale: This omits the constant term: 27+36−15=48. The remainder p(3) also includes +6, so it is 54.
wrong.error_pattern: drops the constant term

wrong.rationale: This computes 3³ as 3·3=9 instead of 27: 9+36−15+6=36.
wrong.error_pattern: treats a power as a product

change_note: New cubic and divisor; distractors use sign, constant term and exponent errors.

title: Remainder Theorem with x + 2
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

When p(x)=3x³−x²+2x−10 is divided by x+2, what is the remainder?

wrong.rationale: This evaluates p(2) instead of p(−2): 24−4+4−10=14. Dividing by x+2 requires evaluating at −2.
wrong.error_pattern: evaluates at the opposite sign

wrong.rationale: This omits the constant term: −24−4−4=−32. The remainder p(−2) also includes −10, so it is −42.
wrong.error_pattern: drops the constant term

wrong.rationale: This computes (−2)³ as +8 instead of −8: 3(8)−4−4−10=6.
wrong.error_pattern: sign error on an odd power

change_note: Divisor x+2 requires evaluating at −2; different polynomial.

title: Remainder Theorem with a missing term
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

When p(x)=2x⁴−5x²+3x+1 is divided by x+1, what is the remainder?

wrong.rationale: This evaluates p(1) instead of p(−1): 2−5+3+1=1. Dividing by x+1 requires evaluating at −1.
wrong.error_pattern: evaluates at the opposite sign

wrong.rationale: This computes (−1)⁴ as −1 instead of 1: −2−5−3+1=−9.
wrong.error_pattern: sign error on an even power

wrong.rationale: This omits the constant term: 2−5−3=−6. The remainder p(−1) also includes +1, so it is −5.
wrong.error_pattern: drops the constant term

change_note: Quartic with no cubic term, divisor x+1, even-power sign error.

title: Rational inequality with a nonstrict sign
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

Solve the inequality (x+7)/(x−4)≥0. Which interval notation gives the solution set?

correct.rationale: The critical values are x=−7 (the quotient is 0 and is included) and x=4 (undefined and excluded). The quotient is positive for x<−7 and for x>4, giving (−∞,−7]∪(4,∞).

wrong.rationale: The intervals are right, but x=4 makes the denominator 0, so the expression is undefined there and 4 must be excluded.
wrong.error_pattern: includes the denominator zero

wrong.rationale: This is the solution of (x+7)/(x−4)≤0. For −7<x<4 the numerator is positive and the denominator is negative, so the quotient is negative.
wrong.error_pattern: chooses the intervals where the quotient is negative

wrong.rationale: The intervals are right, but the inequality is nonstrict, so x=−7, where the quotient equals 0, must be included.
wrong.error_pattern: excludes the numerator zero

change_note: Reversed inequality direction relative to the seed, with different numbers, wording and distractors.

title: Rational inequality with a reversed numerator
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

Find all x satisfying (9−x)/(x+8)≥0.

correct.rationale: The critical values are x=9 (quotient 0, included) and x=−8 (undefined, excluded). For −8<x<9 both 9−x and x+8 are positive, so the quotient is positive; for x<−8 and x>9 it is negative.

wrong.rationale: The interval is right, but x=−8 makes the denominator 0, so the expression is undefined there and −8 must be excluded.
wrong.error_pattern: includes the denominator zero

wrong.rationale: This is the solution of (x−9)/(x+8)≥0. The numerator is 9−x, not x−9, so its sign is reversed: the quotient is negative on these intervals.
wrong.error_pattern: misses that the numerator has a negative x coefficient

wrong.rationale: The interval is right, but the inequality is nonstrict, so x=9, where the quotient equals 0, must be included.
wrong.error_pattern: excludes the numerator zero

change_note: Numerator written as 9−x so the sign pattern flips; endpoint decisions required.

title: Rational inequality with three critical values
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

What is the solution set of the inequality (x−8)(x+4)/(x−9)≤0?

correct.rationale: The critical values are −4 and 8 (zeros, included) and 9 (undefined, excluded). The quotient is negative on x<−4 and on 8<x<9, and equals 0 at x=−4 and x=8.

wrong.rationale: The intervals are right, but x=9 makes the denominator 0, so the expression is undefined there and 9 must be excluded.
wrong.error_pattern: includes the denominator zero

wrong.rationale: This is the solution of the ≥0 inequality. On (−4,8) and on x>9 the quotient is positive, not negative.
wrong.error_pattern: chooses the intervals where the quotient is positive

wrong.rationale: The intervals are right, but the inequality is nonstrict, so the zeros x=−4 and x=8 must be included.
wrong.error_pattern: excludes the numerator zeros

change_note: Three critical values with a factored numerator; endpoints and sign chart needed.

title: Predicted change in water level from a cubic model
stem:
Calculator use is permitted.

A cubic regression models the water level w (in cm) of a reservoir x days after a storm: w=0.31x³−2.2x²+1.45x+9.8. According to the model, what is the change in water level from x=1.5 to x=3.4, to the nearest hundredth?

correct.rationale: w(3.4)−w(1.5)=1.48224−8.07125=-6.58901, so the predicted change is −6.59 cm (a decrease).

wrong.rationale: This subtracts in the wrong order: w(1.5)−w(3.4)=8.07125−1.48224=6.58901. The change from 1.5 to 3.4 is final minus initial, which is negative.
wrong.error_pattern: reverses the subtraction

wrong.rationale: This divides the change -6.58901 by the interval length 1.9, giving the average rate of change -3.46790 cm per day. The question asks for the total change.
wrong.error_pattern: reports the average rate instead of the change

wrong.rationale: This is the model's value at the end of the interval, w(3.4)=1.48224, not the change from x=1.5 to x=3.4.
wrong.error_pattern: reports the final value instead of the change

change_note: Reservoir context, new cubic, and a decreasing result.

title: Predicted change in visitors from a cubic model
stem:
Calculator use is permitted.

A cubic regression models the number of daily visitors V (in hundreds) to a museum x months after it opens: V=−0.18x³+1.4x²−0.9x+12.5. What is the predicted change in V from x=2.2 to x=5.6, to the nearest hundredth?

wrong.rationale: This subtracts in the wrong order: V(2.2)−V(5.6)=15.37936−19.75312=-4.37376. The change from 2.2 to 5.6 is final minus initial.
wrong.error_pattern: reverses the subtraction

wrong.rationale: This divides the change 4.37376 by the interval length 3.4, giving the average rate 1.28640. The question asks for the total change.
wrong.error_pattern: reports the average rate instead of the change

wrong.rationale: This evaluates the model at the interval length instead of at the endpoints: V(3.4)=18.54928. The change is V(5.6)−V(2.2).
wrong.error_pattern: evaluates the model at the difference of the inputs

change_note: Positive change with new coefficients; distractors include evaluating at b−a.

title: Predicted temperature change from a quartic model
stem:
Calculator use is permitted.

A quartic regression models the temperature T (in °C) of a greenhouse x hours after sunrise: T=0.07x⁴−0.9x²+2.3x+15. What is the predicted change in T from x=1.3 to x=3.8, to the nearest hundredth?

wrong.rationale: This divides the change 8.671025 by the interval length 2.5, giving the average rate 3.468410 °C per hour. The question asks for the total change.
wrong.error_pattern: reports the average rate instead of the change

wrong.rationale: This is the predicted temperature at the end of the interval, T(3.8)=25.339952, not the change.
wrong.error_pattern: reports the final value instead of the change

wrong.rationale: This subtracts in the wrong order: T(1.3)−T(3.8)=16.668927−25.339952=-8.671025. The change from 1.3 to 3.8 is final minus initial.
wrong.error_pattern: reverses the subtraction

change_note: Quartic model in a temperature context.

title: Average rate of change of a cubic

For g(x)=2x³−5x, what is the average rate of change from x=0.8 to x=2.3, to the nearest tenth?

title: Average rate of change of a drone's height
stem:
Calculator use is permitted.

A drone's height (in meters) t seconds after launch is d(t)=0.2t⁴−1.5t²+3t. What is the average rate of change of its height from t=0.5 to t=2.5, in meters per second, to the nearest tenth?

wrong.rationale: This averages the two heights, (1.1375+5.9375)/2=3.5375, which is a mean height, not a rate of change.
wrong.error_pattern: averages the outputs instead of finding a slope

wrong.error_pattern: omits division by Δt

wrong.error_pattern: reverses the subtraction in the numerator

title: Decay factor below 1
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

Consider f(x)=400(0.85)^x. Which statement correctly describes the change in f each time x increases by 1?

correct.rationale: The growth factor is 0.85=1−0.15, so each unit of x multiplies f by 0.85, a 15% decrease.

wrong.text: It is reduced by 85%
wrong.rationale: This uses the whole factor as the percent change. Multiplying by 0.85 keeps 85% of the value, so the decrease is 100%−85%=15%.
wrong.error_pattern: reads the factor as the percent decrease

wrong.text: It is raised by 15%
wrong.rationale: The factor 0.85 is less than 1, so the outputs shrink. A 15% increase would use a factor of 1.15.
wrong.error_pattern: treats a factor below 1 as growth

wrong.text: It has 0.15 subtracted from it
wrong.rationale: The change is multiplicative, not additive. Each unit multiplies f by 0.85, so the amount lost shrinks as f gets smaller.
wrong.error_pattern: confuses multiplicative and additive change

change_note: Decay instead of growth; different initial value and rate.

title: Small growth rate as a percent
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

For g(x)=5(1.035)^x, which statement is true?

correct.rationale: The factor is 1.035=1+0.035, and 0.035 as a percent is 3.5%, so g increases by 3.5% per unit.

wrong.text: g increases by 35% per unit
wrong.rationale: This misplaces the decimal: 0.035 is 3.5%, not 35%. A 35% increase would use the factor 1.35.
wrong.error_pattern: converts 0.035 to a percent incorrectly

wrong.text: g increases by 103.5% per unit
wrong.rationale: This uses the entire factor 1.035 as the percent change. The factor includes the original 100%, so the increase is 1.035−1=0.035, or 3.5%.
wrong.error_pattern: reads the factor as the percent increase

wrong.text: g increases by a constant amount of 0.035 per unit
wrong.rationale: The change is multiplicative: each unit multiplies g by 1.035. The amount added grows as g grows (for example, 5(0.035)=0.175 from x=0 to x=1, but more later).
wrong.error_pattern: confuses multiplicative and additive change

change_note: Growth rate with a decimal that has two leading digits to convert.

title: Medication decay in context
stem:
No calculator is permitted.

The amount of a medication in the bloodstream is modeled by A(t)=80(0.6)^t, where A is in milligrams and t is in hours. Which statement is true?

correct.text: The amount decreases by 40% each hour
correct.rationale: The factor 0.6=1−0.4, so each hour the amount is multiplied by 0.6, which is a 40% decrease.

wrong.text: The amount decreases by 60% each hour
wrong.rationale: This uses the whole factor as the percent decrease. Multiplying by 0.6 keeps 60% of the amount, so 40% is lost.
wrong.error_pattern: reads the factor as the percent decrease

wrong.text: The amount decreases by 32 mg each hour, which is 40% of 80 mg
wrong.rationale: This takes 40% of the initial 80 mg as a fixed hourly loss. The 40% applies to the current amount: the loss from t=0 to t=1 is 32 mg, but from t=1 to t=2 it is 40% of 48, or 19.2 mg.
wrong.error_pattern: treats the percent change as a percent of the initial value

wrong.text: The amount decreases by 0.4 mg each hour
wrong.rationale: This treats the 0.4 as a constant amount subtracted each hour. The change is multiplicative: the amount is multiplied by 0.6 each hour.
wrong.error_pattern: confuses multiplicative and additive change

change_note: Medication context with a decay factor; distractor for percent of the initial value.
